# How many ElevenLabs credits does dubbing a 10-minute video actually use?

Disclosure: This article contains an affiliate link. Anicca is an independent ElevenLabs affiliate and may earn a commission if you subscribe through it, at no extra cost to you.

Dubbing is the most expensive way to spend an ElevenLabs credit pool, and the pricing page does not show that cost in minutes the way it does for narration. We re-checked the official pricing page on 19 November 2026 — it was headed as Black Friday pricing that day — and worked the dubbing arithmetic ourselves for one concrete case: a single 10-minute video. The answer depends entirely on which dubbing mode you choose, and in the most expensive mode one short video can spend more than an entire Creator month.

## What does ElevenLabs charge for dubbing, per minute?

On the pricing page we checked on 19 November 2026, all ElevenLabs products draw from one shared monthly credit pool, so credits spent on dubbing are credits that are no longer available for anything else. The page lists dubbing at four different rates, depending on the mode:

- Automatic dubbing with watermark: 2,000 credits per minute.
- Automatic dubbing without watermark: 3,000 credits per minute.
- Dubbing Studio with watermark: 5,000 credits per minute.
- Dubbing Studio without watermark: 10,000 credits per minute.

For comparison, the same page lists text to speech at 1 credit per character, speech to text at 330 credits per minute, Eleven Music at 900 credits per minute, sound effects at 200 credits per generation, and voice changer and voice isolator at 1,000 credits per minute each. Dubbing is therefore not slightly more expensive than the other tools. Even its cheapest mode costs twice as much per minute as voice cleanup, and its most expensive mode costs ten times as much.

## A worked example: one 10-minute video, counted in all four modes

This is our own calculation from the rates above, not a figure quoted from the pricing page. Ten minutes of video, dubbed once, with no re-runs:

- Automatic with watermark: 10 × 2,000 = 20,000 credits.
- Automatic without watermark: 10 × 3,000 = 30,000 credits.
- Dubbing Studio with watermark: 10 × 5,000 = 50,000 credits.
- Dubbing Studio without watermark: 10 × 10,000 = 100,000 credits.

Now set those totals against the monthly pools on the same page. The Free pool is 10,000 credits, so Free cannot finish even the cheapest dub of this video — it covers half of it. The Starter pool is 30,000 credits, so Starter covers exactly one automatic dub without a watermark, or one automatic dub with a watermark with 10,000 credits to spare, and nothing else that month. The Creator pool is 121,000 credits, so Creator covers one Dubbing Studio dub without a watermark with 21,000 credits left, or about six automatic watermarked dubs if dubbing is the only work. The Pro pool is 600,000 credits, which is six Dubbing Studio dubs without a watermark, before any narration, transcription or cleanup touches the same pool.

The comparison that makes the scale clear is transcription. Transcribing that same 10-minute video costs about 3,300 credits at 330 credits per minute — roughly one sixth of the cheapest dub, and roughly one thirtieth of the most expensive one. If your workflow is transcribe, translate the text yourself, and then decide whether a full dub is worth it, the cheap step comes first and the expensive step is a deliberate choice. If you dub first to see how it sounds, you have already spent the pool.

## What happens when the video is longer, or the work repeats?

Dubbing costs scale linearly with minutes, so the honest way to budget is to price your real catalogue, not a single test clip. A 45-minute episode in Dubbing Studio without a watermark is 45 × 10,000 = 450,000 credits — most of a Pro month, for one episode, before re-runs. The same episode dubbed automatically with a watermark is 90,000 credits, which fits inside a Creator month but leaves little room for a second episode.

Re-runs matter for the same reason retakes matter in narration, which we worked through in [how many credits a 10-minute narration actually uses](/blog/elevenlabs-how-many-credits-does-narration-use). A second pass over a section you want to fix is not free headroom in the pool; it is the same per-minute rate spent again on those minutes. Budgeting one full dub plus a partial second pass — say, re-dubbing two minutes of a 10-minute video — is more realistic than budgeting a single perfect pass. In Dubbing Studio without a watermark, that realistic total is 100,000 + 20,000 = 120,000 credits, which is effectively the whole Creator pool for one finished video.

## What did the plans cost on the day we checked?

These are the monthly prices and credit pools shown on the official ElevenLabs pricing page on 19 November 2026, with monthly billing selected. Prices exclude all taxes, levies and duties, as the page itself states.

- Free: $0 per month, 10,000 credits.
- Starter: $6 per month, 30,000 credits, shown that day at $1 for the first month.
- Creator: $22 per month, 121,000 credits, shown that day at $11 for the first month.
- Pro: $99 per month, 600,000 credits.
- Scale: $299 per month, 1.8 million credits, 3 seats.
- Business: $990 per month, 6 million credits, 10 seats.
- Enterprise: custom pricing.

The page that day carried Black Friday pricing, and its own FAQ said the Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale ends on December 1, with the first-month offers marked as running until December 1. Treat the $1 and $11 first-month figures as a dated promotion, not as the price of the plans. The same FAQ noted that during the sale Creator annual costs $99 for the year — again, a sale figure to re-check on the pricing page, not a permanent price. Our earlier guide to [ElevenLabs plans for solo creators](/blog/elevenlabs-plans-for-solo-creators) covers the separate question of where commercial usage rights begin, which matters before credits if you publish the dubbed result.

## How should you budget a dubbing project before you start?

Start with one minute, not ten. Dub a single representative minute in the mode you actually intend to ship — watermark choice included, because that choice alone can multiply the cost by five — and compare the credit balance before and after. That one measured minute, multiplied by your video's length, is a better budget than any headline figure, including ours.

Then decide the watermark and Studio questions before you dub the full video, not after. If the watermarked automatic dub is good enough for a test audience, you have spent 2,000 credits per minute to learn that. If you already know you will ship without a watermark from Dubbing Studio, budget at 10,000 credits per minute from the start and do not let a cheaper test mode talk you into a smaller plan.

Finally, keep the shared pool in view. A month that contains one 10-minute Studio dub without a watermark, one narration project and a few transcription jobs is not a Creator month with headroom — on the numbers above it is a Creator month that is already spent. That is the sequence we recommend in [how to test an AI voice tool before you pay](/blog/how-to-test-ai-voice-tools-before-you-pay): measure on your own material first, count the full month honestly, and only then choose the plan.

[Try ElevenLabs free](https://try.elevenlabs.io/elevenlabs-en-1) on a one-minute clip in your intended dubbing mode first, and check the credit balance before and after. That single measurement tells you which of the four rates above will govern your whole project.

More of our checked guides to voice and audio tools are in the [Labs · Voice & Audio hub](/blog/c/ai-voice-tools).

## Common questions

### Does the watermark really change the credit cost?

Yes, on the pricing we checked. Automatic dubbing is listed at 2,000 credits per minute with a watermark and 3,000 without it, while Dubbing Studio is listed at 5,000 with a watermark and 10,000 without it. The watermark decision is therefore a budget decision, not only a presentation decision.

### Can I dub a short video on the Free plan?

Only a very short one, and only in the cheapest mode. At 2,000 credits per minute, the 10,000-credit Free pool covers at most five minutes of automatic watermarked dubbing if nothing else uses the pool. A 10-minute video does not fit on Free in any mode.

### Is dubbing more expensive than narrating the translation myself?

On credits alone, yes, by a wide margin. Narrating a translated script costs 1 credit per character, while dubbing the same minutes costs 2,000 to 10,000 credits per minute. Whether the time saved is worth that difference depends on your project, but the credit difference itself is not close.

### Which plan fits a weekly dubbed video?

Count it, do not guess it. Four 10-minute videos a month in Dubbing Studio without a watermark is 400,000 credits before re-runs, which points to Pro on pool size alone. The same four videos dubbed automatically with a watermark is 80,000 credits, which fits inside Creator. The mode matters more than the posting schedule.
